body: I checked the Apple (embedded and macOS) changes and they look good to me. This is a great addition.

I had already made a PR to do this with a different approach (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116134) but I suppose merging macos and wayland makes sense.

One thing to note is that compositor luminance updates are already event-based and handled here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/137fa73ed4d71d2e7b3a53e2ab6b2690e1f46149/platform/linuxbsd/wayland/display_server_wayland.cpp#L2043-L2050

I felt that since we don't poll for HDR state, we didn't need to check if any values are actually different since this path is executed too infrequently for that to be a performance concern (and I'm not aware of any other concerns about calling these HDR methods or emitting a signal) and just always emitted the event.

If performance is indeed only reason for checking values changed before calling methods/emitting events, I believe the checks can be removed and the event emitted unconditionally (and maybe place a comment explaining that this code path is executed infrequently so this is not a performance concern). Otherwise I'm okay with the changed in `_window_update_hdr_state`.

I also noticed that toggling HDR enabled/disabled emits the event, if this is the case consider also putting event emission here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/137fa73ed4d71d2e7b3a53e2ab6b2690e1f46149/platform/linuxbsd/wayland/display_server_wayland.cpp#L1866-L1893

I'm not aware of any driver except llvmpipe for which enabling HDR should fail, but if such a driver ever exists emitting the appropriate value when returning to SDR rendering might be appropriate.

Happy with the changes to Wayland code!

Out of curiosity, will this PR be updated to also include Android?
